title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
subtitle: big tender beef meatballs browned, then simmered in marinara, over spaghetti with Parmesan
imageAlt: Spaghetti in red marinara topped with four browned meatballs and grated Parmesan
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen beef? Thaw in the fridge overnight.
Put a big pot of salted water on to boil while you roll the meatballs.
Use a plain or traditional marinara (no visible basil leaves).

steps.title: Soak the crumbs
steps.text: In a big bowl, stir the panko and milk together and let it sit 5 minutes. This 'panade' is the secret to soft, juicy meatballs.

steps.title: Mix and roll
steps.text: Add the beef, eggs, Parmesan, grated onion, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, pepper and garlic powder. Mix gently with your hands just until combined — overmixing makes them tough. Roll into 16 balls (about 5 cm / golf-ball size), wetting your hands so they don't stick.

steps.title: Brown the meatballs
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high. Brown the meatballs in 2 batches, turning, 5–6 minutes per batch until browned all over (they finish in the sauce). Set aside and pour off most of the fat.

steps.title: Simmer in sauce
steps.text: Pour the marinara into the skillet, scrape up the brown bits and bring to a simmer. Nestle the meatballs in, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, turning once, until 71°C (160°F) in the centre.

steps.title: Cook the spaghetti
steps.text: Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in the salted boiling water until al dente (box time, about 9–10 min). Save ½ cup pasta water and drain.

steps.title: Toss and serve
steps.text: Toss the spaghetti with a few ladles of the sauce and a splash of pasta water so it's glossy. Plate, top with meatballs and more sauce, and finish with Parmesan.

fixIt.fix: Let the panade soak fully and chill the rolled meatballs 10 minutes before browning. Turn them gently with tongs.
Mix just until combined and don't pack them tightly when rolling.
Loosen with a splash of the pasta water.
Taste the sauce after simmering and add a pinch of salt — the meatballs soak it up.

saleTip: Ground beef family packs and jarred marinara are both frequent No Frills flyer items — 2 jars for $5 is common.
swap: Half beef, half ground pork for extra tender meatballs (cook to 71°C / 160°F). Bake the meatballs at 200°C (400°F) 18–20 min instead of browning to skip the splatter.
leftovers: Fridge 4 days. Freeze the meatballs in sauce up to 3 months.
source: Based on tested meatball methods (Serious Eats panade technique, America's Test Kitchen): milk-soaked crumbs, gentle mixing, browned then simmered in sauce; ground-beef temp per Health Canada.
gear: Large deep skillet with a lid
prepAhead: Roll the meatballs up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge.
Freeze raw rolled meatballs on a tray, then bag; brown from frozen and add 5 min to the simmer.
reheat: Warm meatballs and sauce covered on the stove over medium-low, or microwave 2–3 min, until 74°C (165°F). Add a splash of water to the pasta.

basic.note: Simple beef meatballs simmered in jarred sauce.

stepNotes.1: Basic: beef, crumbs, milk, eggs, Parmesan, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.

fancy.note: Tender ricotta meatballs, a sauce enriched with butter, and spaghetti tossed until glossy.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: fold the ricotta into the mix — the softest meatballs you'll make.
stepNotes.3: Fancy: stir the butter into the sauce at the end.

plating: Twirl the spaghetti high in a warm bowl.
Three meatballs on top, sauce spooned over them only.

why.0-0: The panko soaked in milk keeps meatballs soft and juicy.
why.0-3: Eggs bind the meatballs so they hold together in the sauce.
why.0-4: Parmesan seasons the meatballs from the inside.
